definition: A certificate authority signs certificates and can delegate signing authority to subordinate authorities.
A certificate binds the identity of its subject to a public key.
A public key is the shareable key of a mathematically related public and private key pair.
A root CA anchors trust for certificates in its hierarchy.
A trust store is a collection of trusted certificate authorities used to validate certificate chains.
A certificate revocation list identifies revoked certificates that clients periodically download and store.
OCSP lets a client query an authoritative database for certificate revocation status.
